title: Equal Rational Numbers
summary: Given two strings s and t, each representing a non-negative rational number with optional repeating parts in parentheses, return true if and only if they represent the same number.
statement: Given two strings s and t, each representing a non-negative rational number with optional repeating parts in parentheses, return true if and only if they represent the same number. A rational number can be in one of three forms: an integer part, an integer part with a non-repeating part, or an integer part with a non-repeating part and a repeating part enclosed in parentheses.
constraints: Each input is a nonnegative decimal with an optional parenthesized repeating suffix.
A missing decimal or repeating part is allowed.
Return whether the two strings represent exactly the same rational number.
hints: Parse integer, finite fractional, and repeating pieces separately.
A repeating r-digit block contributes block/(10^m*(10^r-1)) after m finite digits.
Build exact Fraction values and compare them.
The geometric-series denominator represents the infinite repetition without floating-point rounding.
editorial: The geometric-series denominator represents the infinite repetition without floating-point rounding.

tests.explanation: Both repeating expansions equal fifty-two over ninety-nine.
Both representations repeat digit six after equivalent finite prefixes.
